figures.finding: For tax year 2026-27 (the first under the Income-tax Act, 2025) the default regime taxes total income at nil to ₹4 lakh, then 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% and 25% in ₹4 lakh steps to ₹24 lakh and 30% above, plus surcharge from ₹50 lakh and 4% health and education cess; a resident gets a rebate wiping out the tax up to ₹12 lakh of income (up to ₹60,000). There is no state income tax.

figures.finding: A supplier of services must register for GST once aggregate turnover in a financial year exceeds ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh in a special category State, which the Government may raise up to ₹20 lakh at that State's request); the GST rate on a screen worker's services is not established here.
figures.applies: CGST Act, 2017 s. 22(1) as enacted, with the second proviso inserted by the CGST (Amendment) Act, 2018 (copies hosted by the GST Council); later amendments for goods-only suppliers not read.

figures.finding: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020 the employer pays 10% of wages to the provident fund (12% in establishments the Government notifies) and the employee the same, of which up to 8.33% goes to the pension fund; the wage ceiling for mandatory EPFO coverage and contributions rose from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 a month on 17 September 2026. Under ESI the employer pays 3.25% and the employee 0.75% of wages (from 1 July 2019).
figures.applies: Employees of covered establishments; a self-employed screen worker is outside EPF and ESI. Which establishments are notified for 12% and the ESI wage limit were not read from a primary source; no change to the ESI rates after 2019 was found.
